name: Plato the Younger
bio: Plato the Younger is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors records the poet's date as unknown.
This archive carries the 3 epigrams ascribed to the poet in the third volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Book IX: 13, 748, 751).

poems.title: Book IX, 13
poems.author: Plato the Younger
poems.text: A blind man carried a lame man on his back, lending him his feet and borrowing from him his eyes.

poems.title: Book IX, 748: On Dionysus carved on an Amethyst
poems.author: Plato the Younger
poems.text: The stone is amethyst, but I am the toper Dionysus. Hither let it teach me to be sober, or learn itself to get drunk.

poems.title: Book IX, 751
poems.author: Plato the Younger
poems.text: The stone is Hyacinthus, and on it are Apollo and Daphne. Of which was Apollo rather the lover?
